title: Collector framework + context bundle scaffold (timeouts, concurrency, fail-open)
author: Jacob Stein
description: Implements the initial collector/plugin framework for the incident bot and a minimal scaffold for assembling and posting “context bundles”. This is the foundation for Phase 1+ collectors (recent deploys, config diffs, saturation snapshot) and focuses on reliability guardrails: bounded execution time, concurrency control, and fail-open behavior (partial bundle rendering). Included: Collector interface + result types, BundleAssembler orchestration, global + per-collector timeouts with cancellation, concurrency limiter, structured error reporting per collector, and basic unit tests + CI wiring. Motivation: during incidents we need deterministic bot behavior (no thread spam, no hanging collectors, predictable load on downstream systems) while allowing incremental addition of new collectors over time. Non-goals: implementing actual collectors (deploy/config/saturation), restricted-mode posting, caching/memoization, or “suspected change” heuristics (tracked separately).
commits: incident-bot: introduce Collector interface and CollectorResult (ok/error/timeout) with redaction hooks
incident-bot: add BundleAssembler with ordered sections and partial rendering when collectors fail
infra: implement per-collector timeout + global wall-clock timeout with context cancellation
infra: add concurrency limiter (max parallel collectors) and bounded fan-out
tests: add unit tests for timeout, cancellation propagation, and stable ordering of bundle sections
ci: add lightweight job to run unit tests + lint for incident-bot repo
changed_areas: src/bundles/assembler.ts (new) — orchestrates collectors, formats bundle, handles partials
src/slack/format.ts (touched) — adds minimal block scaffolding for bundle post
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we ensure collector failures don’t look like “no issues found”? Responders need explicit missing-data signals. Also: please avoid adding high-cardinality labels to any internal metrics you add in the framework.

Jacob Stein (author): Updated rendering to include a per-collector status line when error/timeout occurs (e.g., “deploy_collector: timeout after 1200ms”). No metrics emitted in this PR; we’ll add framework metrics with a controlled label set in a follow-up (ENG-2845).

Marcus Lin (security review): Please confirm the framework won’t accidentally serialize request payloads into Slack blocks in error cases (stack traces, raw responses, etc.). Also would like a placeholder for a redaction step even if collectors implement it.

Jacob Stein (author): Good call. Errors are normalized into (code, message) with stack traces stripped by default; raw responses are not stored on CollectorError. Added an optional `redact()` hook on CollectorMetadata; assembler calls it before rendering sections. Actual key allowlists/redaction logic will live in the config diff collector PR.
Sean Gallagher (review): Timeout defaults feel aggressive—what’s the budget? During major incidents we can tolerate partials but not repeated timeouts spamming threads.

Jacob Stein (author): Set defaults to global 2000ms, per-collector 1200ms with a hard cap; also added a single-post per incident update cycle (assembler returns a single bundle object, posting cadence remains unchanged). We can tune defaults once we see deploy/config collector latency distributions.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please add a unit test that ensures collector order is stable regardless of resolution time; responders want consistent muscle memory. Also add a safeguard so one collector can’t starve others under the concurrency cap.

Jacob Stein (author): Added deterministic ordering test; also changed implementation to schedule collectors in declared order while enforcing max concurrency (no starvation; slower collectors don’t block earlier sections from being rendered as long as they complete before global timeout).
Logan Wright (review): For future saturation collector, we’ll need to distinguish “metrics backend delayed” vs “collector error”. Suggest an error taxonomy now so we don’t break formatting later.
Jacob Stein (author): Added CollectorError codes: TIMEOUT, UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, UPSTREAM_INVALID_RESPONSE, PERMISSION_DENIED, INTERNAL. Formatting uses the code + short message (no stack).
release_notes: Internal-only: incident bot now supports a collector/plugin framework with bounded timeouts and concurrency controls; no user-facing behavior change until collectors are enabled.
